p: the check of my reproach: He declares that two things moved him to speak: that is, because Job seemed to touch him, and because he thought he had knowledge sufficient to confute him.
his excellency mount up to the: His purpose is to prove Job to be a wicked man, and a hypocrite, because God punished him, and changed his prosperity into adversity.
seek to please the poor: While the father through ambition and tyranny oppressed the poor, the children through poverty and misery will seek favour from the poor.
restore their goods: So that the thing which he has taken away by violence will be restored again by force.
shall lie down with him in: Meaning that he will carry nothing away with him but his sin.
sweet in his mouth: As poison that is sweet in the mouth brings destruction when it comes into the body: so all vice at the first is pleasant, but God later turns it to destruction.

poison of asps: He compares ill-gotten goods to the venom of asps, which is a dangerous serpent, noting that Jobs great riches were not truly come by and therefore God plagues him justly for the same.
rivers: Though God gives all other abundance from his blessings yet he will have no part of it.

and he shall not rejoice therein: That is these raveners and spoilers of the poor will enjoy their theft but for a time for after God will take it from them, and cause them to make restitution so that it is only an exchange.
meat be left: He will leave nothing to his posterity.
of the wicked shall come upon: The wicked will never be in rest: for one wicked man will seek to destroy another.
and shall rain it upon him: Some read, upon his flesh, alluding to Job, whose flesh was smitten with a scab.
body: Some read, of the quiver.
All darkness shall be hid in: All fear and sorrow will light on him when he thinks to escape.
blown shall consume him: That is, fire from heaven, or the fire of God's wrath.
increase of his house shall depart: Meaning, the children of the wicked will flow away like rivers and be dispersed in various places.
God: Thus God will plague the wicked.
God: Against God, thinking to excuse himself, and to escape God's hand.
